properties.name: With 2–3 Claude Code writers in flight on one hosted design (StoryFlow on flo2.io, 09-29 00:42–01:18 UTC), the median engine write time rose from about 0.25 s to 1.8–3.7 s, and the engine logged 73 search-index "couldn't find segment" warnings during the write bursts. No loss was seen
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-29 by the read-only server-side half of the islands study. Sources: flo2's design_writes (created_at to finished_at per write, joined to the connector call log) and `docker logs reflow2` on the droplet.

WHAT WAS SEEN:
- StoryFlow, 09-29 00:42–01:18 UTC: 28 episodes in which 2 or more writes from Claude Code 2.1.283 were in flight at the gateway together, covering 67 writes. A 2.1.284 process interleaved from 01:06:50 to 01:15:14.
- Median engine write time over those windows: 1.8–3.7 s, against about 0.25 s outside them.
- 73 tantivy "couldn't find segment in SegmentManager" warnings from 00:24 to 04:19, clustered around StoryFlow (59) and graph-primitives (26) write bursts, with a median of 31 writes within ±60 s of each warning.
- The engine twice closed flo2's design "to make room for" StoryFlow (00:50:59, 01:14:41). It runs with --registry-max-open 64.

WHAT IS INFERRED, NOT PROVEN:
- The slowdown is attributed to writes waiting on the store's single write lock. No per-write lock-wait timing exists to confirm it. Idle closes and reopens of other designs in the same window may also contribute.
- The warnings read as a merge-versus-commit race in the search index under a high commit rate. No lost or stale search result was observed, but none was tested for.

WHY IT MATTERS: the only real concurrency measured in a month is one person's parallel subagents (fact:measured-concurrency-across-all-designs-shows-no-lost-work-and-islands-would-mostly-block-a-sessions-own-subagents-2026-09-29), and this is its cost on the hosted engine. The ideal-knowledge-graph design targets 1,000 active users on one engine, so this is the first field number for write contention there.
